section_title: What is the watchman responsible for?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 1 Again the word of the LORD came to me, saying, 2 “Son of man, speak to your people and tell them: ‘Suppose I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land choose a man from among them, appointing him as their watchman, 3 and he sees the sword coming against that land and blows the ram’s horn to warn the people. 4 Then if anyone hears the sound of the horn but fails to heed the warning, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head. 5 Since he heard the sound of the horn but failed to heed the warning, his blood will be on his own head. If he had heeded the warning, he would have saved his life. 6 But if the watchman sees the sword coming and fails to blow the horn to warn the people, and the sword comes and takes away a life, then that one will be taken away in his iniquity, but I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.’

7 As for you, O son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; so hear the word from My mouth and give them the warning from Me. 8 If I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you will surely die,’ but you do not speak out to dissuade him from his way, then that wicked man will die in his iniquity, yet I will hold you accountable for his blood. 9 But if you warn the wicked man to turn from his way, and he does not turn from it, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life.

context_lines: The Lord begins with the familiar work of a watchman. When an enemy approaches, he must sound the warning. A person who hears but refuses to respond bears responsibility for that refusal.
If the watchman sees the danger and remains silent, he too is accountable when someone is taken. The failure of one person does not make the other person’s duty disappear.

The Lord applies the picture to Ezekiel, whom He has made a watchman for Israel. His task is to hear the word from the Lord’s mouth and warn the people. He cannot make them turn, but he must not withhold the warning.
common_interpretation_lines: [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/ezekiel/33.htm) reads the watchman’s work as a duty to warn rather than reassure people who persist in wrongdoing. [Wesley](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/ezekiel/33.htm) understands the person taken by the sword as still accountable for his own sin.

The [USCCB notes](https://bible.usccb.org/bible/ezekiel/33) connect this commission with Ezekiel’s earlier appointment in chapter 3. The renewal prepares the ministry that will now announce restoration, while keeping the seriousness of hearing and responding.
god_plan_lines: [Acts 20:25–32](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/20.htm) gives a related pattern in Paul’s farewell to the elders. He says that he is innocent of everyone’s blood because he did not shrink from declaring God’s whole will. He then calls them to watch over the flock and remember his persistent warnings.

Acts does not explicitly quote Ezekiel here. The wider connection is responsibility for faithfully giving God’s word and caring for those entrusted to one’s care. Paul commits the people to God and the word of His grace; faithful warning belongs with that care.
